title: Light Switches
prompt: There is a light bulb inside a room and four switches outside. All switches are currently off, and exactly one switch controls the bulb. You may flip any switches as many times as you like before entering the room.
Once you enter the room, you can observe the bulb and touch it — but you may only enter once.
How many times do you need to enter the room to identify which switch controls the bulb?
hints: On/off alone distinguishes 2 states — not enough for 4 switches. What other property does a light bulb have beyond on/off?
A bulb that has been on for a while becomes warm. A bulb that is currently on and was recently switched on is bright but cool.
Use two binary signals — on/off and hot/cold — to create four distinct combinations.
solution_lede:
A light bulb has two observable properties: whether it is currently on or off, and whether it is warm or cold. Two binary signals give 2 × 2 = 4 distinct combinations — exactly enough for four switches.

The method: turn on switches 1 and 2. Wait several minutes. Turn off switch 2, turn on switch 3. Then enter the room immediately and observe the bulb:

On and hot → switch 1 (on for a while)
Off and hot → switch 2 (was on, now off)
On and cold → switch 3 (just turned on)
Off and cold → switch 4 (never turned on)

One visit is sufficient.

solution_steps.body: Turn on switches 1 and 2. Wait several minutes for the bulb (if on) to heat up.
Turn off switch 2. Turn on switch 3. Enter the room immediately.
Touch the bulb and observe: on+hot=switch 1, off+hot=switch 2, on+cold=switch 3, off+cold=switch 4.
